financing.summary: PulteGroup is investment grade (Baa1/BBB+/A-) and lightly levered: $1.8B of senior notes, no notes due before 2031, an undrawn $1.75B Bank of America-agented revolver to 2031, and debt-to-capital of 12.1% (3.0% net) at 2026-09-30. It funds land mainly from operating cash flow ($5.2B land spend in 2025, about $5.3B guided for 2026) while buying back about $1.3B of stock a year. It controls 224,275 lots, 54.6% under option. Most options are with land sellers, and land bankers hold only about 7% of controlled lots. Management's stated future mix is about 20% land-banker options (from 7%), 50% seller options and 30% owned. That plan, together with its 70% optioned goal and Fitch tying an upgrade to fewer owned lots, makes Pulte a large and growing land-bank buyer.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, moving lighter. Long-term goal: control 70% of the pipeline through options, with about 3 years of owned land. Mix was 43% owned / 50% seller options / 7% land-banker options at YE2025, and the future goal is about 30% / 50% / 20%. Over 80% of optioned lots are with the underlying land seller, which Pulte calls more flexible and cheaper. Land-banker deals are struck parcel by parcel, each a discrete transaction. Deals are sourced locally and approved centrally against a risk-scored IRR hurdle (18-19% for low-risk projects, 25-30% for high-risk ones). In 2026 Pulte has re-underwritten options and walked away from some (optioned lots 148,663 at mid-2025 to 122,515 at Q3 2026).

lots.source_title: PulteGroup Q3 2026 earnings call slides (2026-10-22), 'Land Pipeline' slide
lots.note: Slide states '224K lots under control, with 55% held via option'; pct_optioned is 122,515 / 224,275. years_supply is our calculation: 224,275 lots / 27,796 trailing-12-month closings (Q4 2025 7,821 + Q1 2026 6,102 + Q2 6,997 + Q3 6,876); owned lots alone = about 3.7 years. Year-end 2025 (10-K): 234,632 controlled, 101,104 owned, 133,528 optioned (56.9%); by segment optioned/controlled: Northeast 7,202/10,873, Southeast 36,519/55,372, Florida 34,345/60,194, Midwest 21,660/31,979, Texas 19,162/35,382, West 14,640/40,832. Peak optioned was 148,663 at 2025-06-30; Pulte has since walked away from option contracts (optioned lots down about 26,000 in 15 months).

land_banking.description: Pulte's own breakdown of lots under control: options with land bankers were about 3% (2023), 6% (2024) and 7% (2025) of controlled lots; it uses 'established land-banking relationships' to option individual parcels, each as a discrete transaction. The stated future mix is about 50% seller options, about 20% land-banker options and about 30% owned.
land_banking.source_title: PulteGroup 2026 Investor Presentation, Raymond James conference (2026-03-02), slide 'Strategic and Efficient Land Option Strategy'
land_banking.note: 7% of 234,632 lots at 2025-12-31 is roughly 16,000 land-banked lots (our calculation from a rounded chart percentage). Reaching ~20% on a ~225,000-lot pipeline would mean ~45,000 land-banked lots, nearly 3x today. Counterparty names are not disclosed. Chart values read from slide text; the 3% label sits on the 2023 column.

land_banking.description: Option contracts with variable interest entities (typically land banks and seller-created entities): $416.5M of deposits and pre-acquisition costs against $3,254.1M remaining purchase price at 2026-09-30. Pulte is not the primary beneficiary of any; none are consolidated. Total options: $1,245.2M deposits, $9,436.4M remaining purchase price.
land_banking.source_title: PulteGroup 10-Q Q3 2026, Note 2 House and Land Inventory (R7)
land_banking.note: VIE option book was $436.3M deposits / $3,307.7M remaining price at 2025-12-31. Deposit write-offs from abandoned options: $23.1M in 9M 2026. Separately, $136.7M 'consolidated inventory not owned' includes land sold to third parties with a Pulte repurchase option.

land_banking.source_title: The Real Deal: Pulte plans 145 homes in Palm Beach County (2024-05-13)
land_banking.note: Older than 24 months; no newer confirmation of further Essential Housing deals with Pulte found. VERIFY 2026-11-19: downgraded from Reported: source is 30 months old and returned 403 to the checker; a 2025 Real Deal piece seen in search describes Pulte as having bought the site, so option vs purchase is unclear.

land_banking.description: New builder relationship: contract for 1,326 homesites in two Bay County, Florida communities, with options that could bring the total to 2,653. Development of the first phase is expected in 2027; it anchors Pulte's new Florida Panhandle Division.
land_banking.source_title: PulteGroup press release: PulteGroup Expands Operations into Northwest Florida (2026-08-03)
land_banking.note: Release says the St. Joe deal was announced 'earlier this year'; exact date and price not in the source opened.

land_banking.description: Del Webb Bridgeland: 190 acres and 672 homesites inside Howard Hughes' 11,500-acre Bridgeland master plan in northwest Houston.
land_banking.source_title: Del Webb press release: Del Webb Announces First Active Adult Community in Bridgeland (2026-02-05)
land_banking.note: Purchase vs option structure not disclosed.

land_banking.description: DiVosta paid $40.3M for 62 Orchid Isles sites in the Avenir master plan (about $650K per site) from Ken Endelson's Kenco Communities. In the same batch, a Hearthstone affiliate bought 60 Orchid Isles sites for $39M; the article does not say for which builder.
land_banking.source_title: The Real Deal: Kenco cashes in on Palm Beach Gardens homesites for $107M (2026-04-10)
land_banking.note: Hearthstone's lots are not publicly tied to Pulte; worth asking about. VERIFY 2026-11-19: source returned 403 to the checker; DiVosta buying 62 Avenir/Orchid Isles lots for $40.3M (Apr 2026) is corroborated by other reports, but Kenco as seller rests on the article headline only.

ma.description: Sold Innovative Construction Group (ICG), its off-site framing business (wall panels, trusses; plants of about 400,000 sq ft in Florida and 200,000 sq ft in South Carolina), bought in 2020 for about $104M. Price not disclosed. Pulte took an $81M pre-tax charge in Q4 2025 and booked a $21.4M gain on the divestiture of manufacturing assets in Q3 2026, so the sale closed by 2026-09-30. Pulte plans to keep buying components from ICG's new owner.
ma.map_impact: No homebuilding, people or lot change. Pulte exits factory ownership and redeploys capital to land and homebuilding; one more step toward a capital-light model.
ma.source_title: HousingWire: Why Builders FirstSource bought ICG and why Pulte sold it (2026-08-03)
ma.note: Closing evidenced by the $21.4M gain in the 10-Q Q3 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/822416/000082241626000043/R6.htm); exact closing day not found.
